tool_input.message:
Eight of the nine repos have a commit on chore/ethos-doctor-warns. Circuit needed none. Nothing is pushed, no PRs. Every commit ends with the `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5` trailer, and no hook blocked or was bypassed. All work was inside `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/ethos-warn` (the repo root is ~/Coding/punt-labs/<repo>).

Doctor was run with the released 4.20.3 binary from each worktree. Eight of the nine show no WARN or FAIL lines; points still shows two hook-currency WARNs (below).

**Item 1: team-registry submodule dropped (`git rm --cached .punt-labs/ethos`, `.gitmodules` removed)**

Each `.gitmodules` held only the ethos stanza, so I `git rm`'d the whole file. Each commit is `chore(ethos): drop the retired team-registry submodule` and deletes `.gitmodules` and the 160000 gitlink `.punt-labs/ethos`.

| Repo | SHA | Other files changed | CHANGELOG lint |
|---|---|---|---|
| anthropic-sdk-pharo | ce47789 | `.gitignore` (all 5 lines added), `CHANGELOG.md` (new `### Changed` under Unreleased) | 0 issues |
| claude-agent-sdk-smalltalk | f1ea8a4 | `.gitignore` (4 lines added; also removed the stale comment "# .punt-labs/ managed via git submodule (punt-labs/team)"), `CHANGELOG.md` (bullet in existing `### Changed`) | 0 issues |
| langlearn | 717ab0c | `.gitignore` (4 lines), `CHANGELOG.md` (bullet in existing `### Changed`) | 0 issues |
| postern | af76708 | `.gitignore` (all 5 lines) | no CHANGELOG.md in the repo |
| refactory | 6ee5b85 | `.gitignore` (4 lines), `CHANGELOG.md` (bullet in existing `### Changed`) | 0 issues |
| use-cases | 1f89cf0 | `.gitignore` (4 lines), `CHANGELOG.md` (new `### Changed` under Unreleased) | 0 issues |

- **`.gitignore` lines:** where `.punt-labs/**/*.local.*` already existed (smalltalk, langlearn, refactory, use-cases) I did not duplicate it. I added the other four ethos local-zone lines under the comment "# ethos local zone (runtime state, never committed)".
- **Main checkouts:** I did not touch the submodule's working-tree directory in any of them.

**Item 2: beads and circuit**
- **beads:** SHA 1824d0ddf, `chore(ethos): ignore local extension files`. It changes `.gitignore` (adds `.punt-labs/**/*.local.*`) and `CHANGELOG.md` (new `### Changed` under Unreleased). Doctor before the change showed the WARN "no .gitignore rule for .punt-labs/**/*.local.*", and it is gone after. The CHANGELOG lint is not clean, but not because of my entry. beads has no markdownlint config, and the file has about 1169 existing findings, mostly MD013 line length and MD024 duplicate headings. My entry is wrapped to 80 columns. Adding a second `### Changed` heading makes one later `Changed` heading a new MD024 duplicate; that is the only finding my entry adds.
- **circuit:** no commit. `origin/main` already has `.gitignore:36 .punt-labs/**/*.local.*`. Doctor from the worktree reports "Local extension files PASS ignored and untracked". It also shows two FAILs: "Audit seal hook: enabled here but no pre-commit hook" and "Audit trailer hook: enabled here but no commit-msg hook". Both mean `ethos enable` has not been run for this worktree's hooks. This is not a tracked-tree issue, and I did not fix it.

**Item 3: points**
- **Commit:** 067aec4, `chore(ethos): remove retired registry leftovers`.
- **Files changed:** `git rm` of `.punt-labs/ethos/.biff`, `.punt-labs/ethos/README.md` and `.punt-labs/ethos/ethos.yaml`, plus a `### Removed` entry in `CHANGELOG.md`. CHANGELOG lint: 0 issues.
- **Precondition:** `.punt-labs/ethos.yaml` exists on the branch (`agent: claude`, `team: gstack`, `active_bundle: gstack`).
- **README.md:** I read it before deleting. It is the retired punt-labs/team README (a submodule description plus how to add a team member), so I removed it and created no `.docs/ethos-registry.md`.
- **Doctor:** the "Unclassified files" WARN is gone. Two WARNs remain, neither in scope:
  - `Seal hook currency  WARN  Seal hook section content differs from what this ethos build would install (installed sha256:e7cacc3c, current sha256:564cd7ee) — run ethos enable to refresh`
  - `Trailer hook currency  WARN  Trailer hook section content differs from what this ethos build would install (installed sha256:ed7daa4e, current sha256:705f7089) — run ethos enable to refresh`
  - Both clear when someone runs `ethos enable` on the host.

**Lint invocation:** I ran markdownlint as `bash -c 'cd <worktree> && npx markdownlint-cli2 CHANGELOG.md'`, because run from the ethos cwd it would apply that repo's config.

tool_input.message:
install.sh now builds fuzz with `-std=gnu17`, and `make check` passes. Commit 7754bde is on chore/ethos-enable-refresh; I did not push. I could not reproduce the CI failure itself, because this host's gcc is 13.3, which lacks `-std=c23`.

**The flag goes to `make`, not `configure`.** fuzz's `src/Makefile.in` hardcodes `CC=gcc` and never substitutes `CFLAGS`. My first attempt, `CFLAGS=` passed to configure, was silently dropped (the compile lines showed no `-std`). Passing it as `make CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:-} -std=gnu17"` takes effect. The second `make` invocation inside `make install` finds nothing to rebuild, so one flag site is enough.

**Changes:**
- **`install.sh`:** the `make` call becomes `make CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:-} -std=gnu17" || {`, with a comment naming the C23 `bool` keyword and why it must go to make. A caller's CFLAGS stay in front. Apple clang accepts `-std=gnu17`; I could not run that here.
- **`tests/test_install_fuzz_scratch.py`:**
  - The existing `make` assertion now expects two calls: the first with CFLAGS ending in ` -std=gnu17`, then `install`.
  - A new test `test_make_pins_a_pre_c23_dialect` is parametrized on empty and `-O2 -g` caller CFLAGS. It asserts the exact `CFLAGS=` argument.
- **`tests/test_install_sh_output.py`:** same `make` assertion update, which the change had broken.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** an entry under Unreleased `### Fixed`.

**Verification:**
- **Pre-C23 build, `--fuzz-only`:** a sandbox run (`HOME=.tmp/home-new2`, `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, `CFLAGS=-std=c2x`) compiled with `gcc -std=c2x -std=gnu17 -Wall -c ...` and installed fuzz.
- **Reproducing the C23 error:** gcc 13 with `-std=c2x` rejects `typedef int bool;` (exit 1). With `-std=c2x -std=gnu17` it compiles (exit 0). Because the later `-std` wins, appending gnu17 is the right order.
- **Not tested:** a gcc 15 default-C23 build; this host has gcc 13.3.
- **`make check`:** exit 0. markdownlint, ruff, shellcheck (`install.sh` clean), rulesync, mypy, pyright, fuzz, pytest (726 passed, 6 deselected), probcli, oo and suppression gates all passed. An earlier mid-edit hook run failed 6 tests; those were the stale assertions I then fixed.

Scratch files remain in the worktree's `.tmp/` (`home-new`, `home-new2`, `b.c`); it is gitignored.

Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md (main hooks reference; the page is about 284k characters, so I read it in slices). Quotes below come from WebFetch extraction, not the raw page, so verify exact wording before relying on it. Subagent and MCP-matcher details are from the first slice and the MCP section. Hooks guide: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md. MCP: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md.

(1) updatedInput on MCP tool calls

Yes, PreToolUse can rewrite tool input. Shape from the docs' example:

{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "allow",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "My reason here",
    "updatedInput": { "field_to_modify": "new value" },
    "additionalContext": "..."
  }
}

The field table says: "Modifies the tool's input parameters before execution. Replaces the entire input object, so include unchanged fields alongside modified ones." It also says: "Combine with "allow" to auto-approve, or "ask" to show the modified input to the user. For "defer", ignored." So:
- Replacement, not merge. Send the full tool_input back.
- Combining with "allow" is the documented pattern. The docs do not state that updatedInput is valid without a permissionDecision, and I found no statement that it is rejected alone. Omitting permissionDecision is not documented as behaving any particular way. Treat "not documented" as the answer for the alone case and test it.
- Permission rules are evaluated against the returned input, not the original.
- The docs say AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode need updatedInput paired with "allow", and "allow" alone is not sufficient for them.
- The docs' updatedInput example for the PermissionRequest event uses a different, nested shape (under decision). Do not copy it into PreToolUse.

(2) PreToolUse stdin fields

Common input fields table includes session_id ("Current session identifier"). agent_id: "Unique identifier for the subagent or in-process teammate the hook fires in." agent_type: "Agent name (for example, "Explore" or "security-reviewer"). Present when the session uses --agent or the hook fires inside a subagent." The docs also say: "When a subagent calls a tool, tool events such as PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire the same configured hooks as in the main conversation, and the input carries the agent_id and agent_type common input fields that identify the subagent." PreToolUse adds tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id. Main-thread examples do not show agent_id or agent_type, so for main-thread calls they should be treated as absent. Exact field presence for main-thread calls is not otherwise documented in what I read.

(3) Matching MCP tools by regex

Yes. Matcher rules: names with only letters, digits, _, -, spaces, commas, and \| are exact matches. Anything else is a JavaScript regular expression, unanchored, so it matches anywhere in the value. Use ^...$ for a whole-string match. MCP tools are named mcp__<server>__<tool>. The docs' examples: "mcp__memory__.*" matches all tools from the memory server, and "mcp__.*__write.*" matches write-prefixed tools from any server. The docs warn that "mcp__memory" without .* is an exact string and matches nothing. Plugin-bundled servers use the scoped form mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>, so a matcher like "mcp__plugin_ethos_self__.*" should match. This is my reading of the extraction, not a verbatim quote; confirm against the MCP section. Omitting the matcher or using "*" matches all tools.

Caveats: updatedInput replaces the whole input (no merge); "allow" pairing is the documented pattern and omission-alone is not documented; agent_id and agent_type are documented for subagent calls only.

tool_input.content:
# MCP identity under Claude Code

Claude Code gives an MCP server no session or agent identity: the server's
environment carries no `CLAUDE_PID`, and the MCP request names no caller. Ethos
therefore learns the caller from its own PreToolUse hook (DES-074, amendment
2026-11-03).

## How it works

Before every call to an ethos MCP tool (`mcp__plugin_ethos_self__*` and
`mcp__plugin_ethos-dev_self__*`), `ethos hook pre-tool-use` returns
`updatedInput`: the original arguments plus one reserved argument, `_caller`.

```json
{"_caller": {"session_id": "<hook payload session_id>", "agent_id": "<key>"}}
```

`agent_id` is the payload's `agent_id` when a subagent is calling, so a subagent
resolves to its own persona and not its leader's. For the leader it is the
hook's own corroborated `CLAUDE_PID`, the key `SessionStart` wrote for the
primary participant. The hook overwrites any `_caller` the model supplied. It
returns no `permissionDecision`, so permission rules apply as they would
without the hook. If the payload has no `session_id`, or no agent key can be
determined, the hook adds nothing.

## What the server does with it

`identity whoami`, `session roster` without a `session_id`, `session iam`,
mission binding (`mission create`, `close`, `abandon`), and the Human identity
row of `doctor` resolve the caller from `_caller` through the same
exact-participant path as the OpenCode pilot (`docs/opencode-mcp-identity.md`):
the roster for `session_id` must exist and hold exactly one participant with
that `agent_id`. Otherwise the call fails with a named error. The server never
falls back to the environment, the process tree, git, or the OS user.

- `session_id` and `agent_id` must each be nonempty and contain only ASCII
  letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. Any other key, type, or value is an
  error.
- An explicit `session_id` argument keeps its meaning as an administrative
  target for `roster`, `join`, and `leave`; `_caller` does not override it.
- `iam` changes only the declared caller's own participant, and refuses a
  different `session_id` or `agent_id`.
- Without `_caller` (a client other than Claude Code, or no hook) behavior is
  unchanged.

`_caller` identifies the caller for routing. It is not authentication: any
client that can send arguments can send it. The hook is what makes it
trustworthy under Claude Code.

## Nested sessions

A `claude -p` started from a session's shell inherits that session's
`CLAUDE_PID`, and so does its MCP server. Before this change the nested
session's `session roster` returned the outer session's roster. The hook payload
carries the nested session's own `session_id`, so the server now answers for the
nested session.

## Hook wrappers

The wrappers in `plugin/hooks/*.sh` pass stdin to the ethos binary unmodified.
They used to read one line with `read -r -t 1`, which cut a large payload (an
Edit of a large file) at 8 KiB when the writer paused, and logged `invalid JSON
input (8192 bytes)`. The ethos binary bounds its own wait.

Mission m-2026-11-03-007 is implemented in four commits on fix/mcp-caller-hook, and the round-1 result is submitted (verdict pass). Nothing is pushed. I found no contradiction between the DES-074 amendment and the code.

## Commits
- 2ed8f81 fix(hooks): forward hook stdin to ethos unmodified
- 5755cb2 feat(mcp): resolve a hook-declared caller through the exact-participant path
- dcd5d2c feat(hook): declare the caller on ethos MCP tool calls
- 750b2d5 docs: MCP identity under Claude Code; changelog

## make check
`make check` exited 0 on each of the four commits. I ran it with output redirected to `.tmp/check.out` because the output is huge, then grepped for FAIL (0 hits); the file ends at the "fuzz docs/spec-hook-gates.tex" line and "make: Leaving directory". On the last run, `internal/hook` was 63s, `internal/mcp` 10s and `plugin/hooks` 4.5s, all ok.

## Behaviour
- **Hook:** `internal/hook/pretooluse_caller.go` handles calls matching `^mcp__plugin_ethos(-dev)?_self__`. The existing gates run first, and a deny stands.
  - Otherwise it returns `updatedInput` (the original arguments plus `_caller {session_id, agent_id}`) with no `permissionDecision`. The agent_id is the payload's, else the corroborated CLAUDE_PID.
  - It always overwrites a model-supplied `_caller`. With no session_id or no agent key it falls back to the old output (`allow`, no `updatedInput`).
  - `permissionDecision` is now `omitempty`. Agent, Write and Edit output is unchanged.
- **Server:** `internal/mcp/caller.go` gains `requestCaller`, which reads `_meta` (opt-in, as before) or `_caller`; `_caller` is always on.
  - It validates with the same safe-ID pattern as `_meta`, rejects unknown keys, and refuses a request carrying both sources.
  - `callerParticipant(ref)` now matches the exact `agent_id`; the `_meta` path is just `agent_id == session_id`.
  - Whoami, `resolveSessionID` (roster/join/leave/iam), iam, mission bind/clear (new `callerSessionID`) and the doctor "Human identity" row all use it. Without `_caller` the old chain runs unchanged.
  - `callerOption()` adds `_caller` to the identity, session, doctor and mission schemas with the description "Set by the ethos hook; do not supply."
  - `bindDispatchedMission` and `clearClosedMissionBindings` now take `req`; I updated the two existing tests that call them.
- **Wrappers:** all 8 `plugin/hooks/*.sh` now run `ethos hook X` directly on stdin. The kill switch and missing-binary bypasses are kept, shellcheck is clean, and a comment explains the change.
- **Docs:** CHANGELOG Unreleased "Fixed" has three entries, and `docs/claude-code-mcp-identity.md` is new.

## Tests and fail-before
- **Wrapper test:** `plugin/hooks/stdin_wrappers_test.go` runs each wrapper with stdin on a socketpair (what Node gives a child) and a fake `ethos` that records the bytes.
  - **`TestWrappersForwardStalledPayloadIntact`:** the writer sends 8 KiB, pauses 1.3s, then sends the rest. Before the fix every wrapper forwarded 8193 of 102452 bytes, the same 8192-byte signature as production. It passes after.
  - **`TestWrappersForwardMultilinePayload`:** failed before for all 8 wrappers (cut at the first newline); passes after.
  - **`TestWrappersForwardLargePayloadIntact`:** a 100 KiB single line passes before and after on Linux bash 5.2. The truncation needs a writer that stalls past 1s; an unstalled 100 KiB write does not reproduce it. Please do not claim the unstalled case was fixed.
  - **`TestWrappersBypasses`:** kill switch and no-config bypass.
- **MCP tests:** `internal/mcp/caller_hook_test.go` has the `TestDeclaredCaller_*` set.
  - **Coverage:** leader keyed on CLAUDE_PID, subagent resolves its own persona, nested session beats an inherited outer env, no fallback on a wrong participant or session, 16 malformed variants across whoami/roster/iam/doctor, explicit session_id as admin target (roster/join/leave), iam isolation, both sources refused, doctor, mission session, and schema entries.
  - **Fail-before:** run against a pre-change tree extract (`.tmp/pristine`, `callerArg` and `callerSessionID` stubbed so it compiles), whoami returned the env persona "bob" instead of alice/carol, malformed callers were accepted, and so on.
- **Hook tests:** `internal/hook/pretooluse_caller_test.go` has the `TestPreToolUse_*` set.
  - **Coverage:** leader, subagent, spoof overwritten, no session_id, no agent key, uncorroborated PID, tool-name matching including dev prefix and lookalikes, deny stands, verifier read-only call, and Write/Edit/Read unchanged.
  - **Fail-before:** against the pre-change tree the hook returned `permissionDecision: allow` with no `updatedInput`.
- **Demo:** the real binary built to `.tmp/ethos` and fed a payload with a spoofed `_caller` returned `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","updatedInput":{"_caller":{"agent_id":"agent-x","session_id":"s-1"},"method":"roster"}}}`. I did not run a nested `claude -p`.

## Leader notes
- **Wrapper cause:** the fix is as specified, but ethos's own wait is still 1s (`ReadInput(r, time.Second)`). A stall over 1s truncates inside Go too. Raising that timeout would be cheap, since a complete JSON value returns early; I left it out of scope.
- **Behaviour change:** `permissionDecision: allow` is no longer returned for ethos MCP calls that get a `_caller`. This follows your contract and the amendment's "permissions are unchanged".
- **Trust:** `_caller` is honoured by the server regardless of the OpenCode opt-in, so a client without the hook can spoof it, as with `_meta`. Say so in DES-074 if it is not already clear.
- **Legacy-keyed participants:** a pre-upgrade leader whose roster participant is keyed on the legacy walk PID gets a named "participant not found" error, not the legacy fallback. This is exact-match, as the amendment says.
- **DES-029:** it records that Go cannot read the inherited stdin fd. The wrappers no longer rely on that, because `readWithTimeout` handles it. A one-line note in DES-029 would stop that text misleading later readers. I did not edit DESIGN.md.
- **Review-agent notes:** the PostToolUse hook ran a full `make check` on every Go edit, so the Edit output was noisy mid-change. ## Commits (after 750b2d5)
- 3feaee8 fix(hook): wait up to 10s for a stalled hook payload
- 1f960ff fix(hook)!: stop auto-approving tool calls

The first commit also changed the other seven `ReadInput` callers. The 1f960ff commit carries the `pretooluse.go` timeout line too, because that file also holds the security change and I cannot split hunks interactively. `make check` exited 0 on the final tree and after each change (output redirected to `.tmp/check.out`; no FAIL).

## 1. Security: no auto-approve
- **Fix:** `preToolUsePass` and `preToolUsePassWithEnv` replace the allow variants and emit only `hookEventName` (plus `additionalEnv` on the spawn path). Every pass-through path therefore emits no `permissionDecision`: plain tools, the verifier-inside-allowlist case, Tier A/B Agent spawns, the ethos MCP fallback and the existing-gate result. `deny` is unchanged.
- **Real binary:** `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash",...}' | .tmp/ethos hook pre-tool-use` now prints `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse"}}`.
- **New test:** `TestPreToolUse_PassThroughNeverDecidesPermission` covers Bash, Read, Write, Edit, ethos MCP, other MCP and Agent. `TestPreToolUse_VerifierInsideAllowlistPassesThrough` covers a verifier call inside the allowlist.
  - **Fail-before:** on the unfixed code all seven cases emitted `"permissionDecision":"allow"`, and the verifier case did too.
- **Existing tests:** about 80 assertions that expected `"allow"` now expect no decision, in `pretooluse_test.go`, `pretooluse_dispatch_test.go`, `pretooluse_flock_unix_test.go` and the caller tests. All `deny` assertions are untouched. One test reused a decoded struct across calls (`EnvVarFromSubagentStart`), so I reset it between calls; omitted keys do not overwrite a stale `"deny"`.
- **`additionalEnv`:** it is an ethos-defined field, not a documented Claude Code PreToolUse output field. I could not reach code.claude.com (no web tool), so I could not confirm that against the docs. The code comments (`pretooluse_dispatch.go` around line 895) say `additional_env` does not persist into hook processes, and ethos carries the delegation binding in sidecar files instead. The env block rides the same decision-free output and ethos's own consumers do not depend on a decision.
- **CHANGELOG:** a "Security" entry says ethos no longer auto-approves tool calls.

## 2. Hook stdin wait
- **Constant:** `hookInputTimeout = 10 * time.Second` in `internal/hook/stdin.go`, with a justifying comment. All 8 `ReadInput(r, time.Second)` sites use it.
- **Second cause found:** with the old file-reader (pollable pipe) path, raising the constant alone would not have helped. After each chunk it reset the deadline to `timeout/10`, so with a 10s timeout a stall over 1s still truncated. I replaced that with one overall deadline plus an early return once the buffer is a complete JSON value. `readWithTimeout`, the blocking-fd path, already worked this way.
- **Trade-off:** a hook given no input on an open stdin now waits up to 10s instead of 1s. Claude Code always writes the payload, so this should not occur in practice.
- **Tests:** `TestReadInput_StallMidPayload` feeds the Go reader directly. A writer sends 8 KiB, stalls 1.3s, then sends the rest, with the pipe left open. It covers a pollable `os.Pipe` and a blocking inherited fd.
  - **Fail-before:** the pollable subtest failed with "invalid JSON input (8192 bytes)". The blocking-fd subtest passed before and after, as a regression guard.
- **Constant test:** `TestHookInputTimeoutOutlastsAStall` checks the constant is at least 5s.
- **CHANGELOG:** the Fixed section has an entry for the longer wait.

## For your DESIGN amendments
- **Behaviour change:** ethos MCP calls that get a `_caller` no longer carry an "allow" either, which matches the amendment's "permissions unchanged".
- **DES-054:** the Tier A/B description should say "allow" now means pass-through with no decision, and that only deny is emitted by ethos.
- **Stdin timeout:** hooks now wait 10s overall, with early return on complete JSON. DES-029's "shell reads stdin" rationale is superseded for the wrappers.
- **Scratch files:** `.tmp/pristine`, `head.tar` and `ethos` are in the gitignored `.tmp/`.

**Finding 1, Medium-High: a model-supplied `_caller` is honoured when the hook cannot determine a caller.**
- Location: internal/hook/pretooluse_caller.go:37-40. When `caller == nil`, `handleEthosMCPCall` writes the gate output unchanged. No `updatedInput` is emitted, so the model's original `tool_input`, including any `_caller` it supplied, reaches the server.
- Why it matters: the server (internal/mcp/caller.go `requestCaller`) trusts `_caller` whenever it is present. That happens when `session_id` is absent, or when there is no `agent_id` and `CLAUDE_PID` is uncorroborated. A model can then name any roster participant, such as a leader or another subagent, and have `whoami`, `iam` and mission binding resolve as that participant.
- Contract conflict: the contract says "model-supplied _caller always overwritten", and amendment point 3 says the same.
- Test gap: `TestPreToolUse_NoCallerNoInjection` (internal/hook/pretooluse_caller_test.go:87-107) uses inputs that carry no `_caller`, so this path is untested.
- Fix: when the hook cannot determine a caller and `tool_input` contains `_caller`, emit `updatedInput` with `_caller` removed, or deny. Add a test with a spoofed `_caller` for each of the three no-caller cases (no `session_id`, no agent key, uncorroborated `CLAUDE_PID`).
- A server-side backstop is not an option: the server cannot tell a hook-injected `_caller` from a model-supplied one.

**Low findings**
- internal/hook/stdin.go:60-66 and the `readWithTimeout` goroutine (about lines 100-110) run `json.Valid` on the whole accumulated buffer after every chunk. That is quadratic in the number of chunks. With 64 KiB chunks this is negligible, so no change is needed. Noted for completeness.
- The 10s `hookInputTimeout` is now shared by every handler: SessionStart, SubagentStart/Stop, PreToolUse, PreCompact, SessionEnd, audit-log and format_output. A complete JSON value or EOF returns immediately, so the full wait is paid only when the payload never completes while the pipe stays open. Claude Code always writes the payload and closes or completes it, so I found no real path that stalls. A truncated, never-completed payload on a held-open pipe would block PreToolUse for 10s. I judge that acceptable.

**Checks that passed**
1. No `permissionDecision` other than "deny". The only emission is internal/hook/pretooluse.go:51-52, in `preToolUseDeny`. `PermissionDecision` is `omitempty`, and the pass helpers (`preToolUsePass`, `preToolUsePassWithEnv`) set none. Tier A (pretooluse_dispatch.go:701, 710) and Tier B (:919) use `preToolUsePassWithEnv`. No leftover allow helpers remain. `handleEthosMCPCall` checks the gate's decision and lets a deny stand over injection. `TestPreToolUse_PassThroughNeverDecidesPermission` and `TestPreToolUse_DenyStandsOverInjection` guard this.
2. Hook injection otherwise matches the contract.
   - The regex is `^mcp__plugin_ethos(-dev)?_self__`.
   - `updated` is a full copy of `tool_input` plus `_caller`, always overwritten (pretooluse_caller.go:41-47).
   - `agent_id` comes from the payload, else `ClaudePIDFromEnvCorroborated`; with neither, nothing is injected.
   - Tests cover a leader call, a subagent call (not the leader's key), an overwritten spoof when a caller exists, and no `session_id`, no agent key, and an uncorroborated PID.
3. Server side:
   - `requestCaller` (internal/mcp/caller.go:53-73) refuses when both `_meta` and `_caller` are present.
   - `parseCallerArg` validates with `callerSessionPattern`, requires both IDs and rejects unknown keys.
   - `callerParticipant` requires an exact roster and exact participant, and has no fallback.
   - Wired methods are `whoami`, `iam` (`handleIam`, including the `session_id`/`agent_id` mismatch checks), session `roster`/`join`/`leave` via `resolveSessionID`, mission bind and clear via `callerSessionID` (mission_tools.go), and doctor "Human identity" via `declaredCallerResult`.
   - An explicit `session_id` still targets another session, except for `iam`, which must match.
   - Env, PID and global-store fallbacks are reachable only when `_caller` is absent (tools.go:253-259 and 324).
   - I found no caller-dependent MCP method that skips `_caller`. `join` and `leave` take `agent_id` as an explicit argument, so they are administrative, not self-keyed.
   - Schemas carry `callerOption()` on the identity, session, mission and doctor tools.
4. The wrappers pass stdin unmodified (checked in `pre-tool-use.sh` and `session-start.sh`; the other wrappers have the same diff shape and tests). The kill-switch and missing-binary bypasses are kept. `TestWrappersForwardLargePayloadIntact`, `...StalledPayloadIntact`, `...MultilinePayload` and `TestWrappersBypasses` cover them. The Go reader has one overall deadline and returns early on a complete JSON value, in both `readFromFile` and `readWithTimeout`. `TestReadInput_StallMidPayload` covers both a pollable pipe and a blocking inherited fd with a 1.3s stall.
5. A re-introduced allow, or a merge instead of replace, would be caught: the leader-call test asserts the exact `updatedInput` map and `NotContains permissionDecision`. A fallback would be caught by `TestDeclaredCaller_NoFallback`. The one gap is Finding 1.
6. Go standards are fine: errors wrap with `%w`, doc comments start with the name, and I found no dead code.

func TestDeclaredCaller_PersonaLessWhoami(t *testing.T) {
	h := hookHandler(t)
	t.Setenv("CLAUDE_PID", "4242")
	t.Setenv("ETHOS_SESSION", "sess-lead")
	t.Setenv("ETHOS_AGENT_ID", "4242")
	t.Setenv("USER", "bob")

	result, text := whoami(t, h, map[string]any{callerArg: declared("sess-lead", "agent-gp")})
	require.False(t, result.IsError, text)
	assert.Contains(t, text, "no ethos identity")
	assert.Contains(t, text, "general-purpose")
	for _, other := range []string{"alice", "bob", "carol"} {
		assert.NotContains(t, text, other, "must not fall back to another identity")
	}

	t.Run("without agent_type it names the agent_id", func(t *testing.T) {
		require.NoError(t, h.sessionStore.Join("sess-lead", session.Participant{AgentID: "agent-bare", Parent: "4242"}))
		result, text := whoami(t, h, map[string]any{callerArg: declared("sess-lead", "agent-bare")})
		require.False(t, result.IsError, text)
		assert.Contains(t, text, "agent-bare")
	})
}

func TestDeclaredCaller_PersonaLessIam(t *testing.T) {
	h := hookHandler(t)
	c := declared("sess-lead", "agent-gp")

	result, err := h.handleSession(context.Background(), callTool(map[string]any{
		"method": "iam", "persona": "missing", callerArg: c,
	}))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, result.IsError, "an unknown persona is still refused")

	result, err = h.handleSession(context.Background(), callTool(map[string]any{
		"method": "iam", "persona": "bob", callerArg: c,
	}))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.False(t, result.IsError, resultText(t, result))
	roster, err := h.sessionStore.Load("sess-lead")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "bob", roster.FindParticipant("agent-gp").Persona)
	assert.Equal(t, "general-purpose", roster.FindParticipant("agent-gp").AgentType, "agent_type is kept")
	assert.Equal(t, "alice", roster.FindParticipant("4242").Persona, "its leader's persona does not change")

	_, text := whoami(t, h, map[string]any{callerArg: c})
	assert.Equal(t, "bob", handleOf(t, text))
}

### Callers with no persona

A participant whose `persona` is empty is a built-in subagent such as
`general-purpose` or `Explore`: `SubagentStart` found no ethos identity named
for its `agent_type` (DES-007, "Null persona handling"). It is a valid caller
with no identity, not an error.

- `identity whoami` returns the text `<agent_type> has no ethos identity`, or
  `<agent_id> has no ethos identity` when the roster recorded no `agent_type`.
  It does not return the leader's, the environment's, or the OS user's identity.
- `session roster` and mission binding act on the caller's session as for any
  caller.
- `session iam` lets the caller declare a persona for its own participant; the
  persona must name an existing identity.
- `doctor` shows the same text on its Human identity row, status PASS.

The convention that maps an `agent_type` to a persona is DES-007's: an identity
whose handle equals the `agent_type`, matched when the subagent starts. Repo
config holds no other `agent_type` mapping.

VERDICT: ACCEPT (no blocking findings; 4 minor findings and 2 DESIGN.md text proposals below).

Tests: `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/mcp/... ./plugin/hooks/...` gives ok internal/mcp 8.489s and ok plugin/hooks 2.116s. shellcheck on all 8 wrappers is clean (no output). `git status` in the worktree is clean. I did not run `make check`.

ADRs read: DES-007 (DESIGN.md:288, null persona at :368, "Persona Default by Agent Type" at :445), DES-029 (:1855), DES-074 (:7903). I did not read DES-061 R4 or the DES-074 2026-11-03 amendment in full. I only saw the first ~200 lines of DES-074, so the amendment text and R4 are unchecked. Nothing in the diff conflicts with what I read.

**1. DES-029 wrappers**
- All 8 wrappers (audit-log, pre-compact, pre-tool-use, session-end, session-start, subagent-start, subagent-stop, suppress-output) have the same three-line body, e.g. plugin/hooks/audit-log.sh:8-10.
  - `HOOK_INPUT=""` is set before the read.
  - `IFS= read -r -d "" -t 10 HOOK_INPUT 2>/dev/null || true`
  - `printf '%s\n' "$HOOK_INPUT" | ethos hook <event> 2>>log || true`
- No wrapper hands the inherited fd to Go. A grep for `ethos hook` and `/dev/stdin` under plugin/ finds only these printf pipes. commit-msg.sh is a git hook and not part of this change.
- The kill-switch, missing `~/.punt-labs/ethos` and missing-binary bypasses (lines 3-5 of each file) are untouched. TestWrappersBypasses covers the first two.
- `read -d ""` with no NUL in the payload and stdin closing: the read hits EOF and returns 1, but bash keeps the data in the variable. I confirmed on bash 5.2.21: `printf '{"b":2}' | { IFS= read -r -d "" -t 10 H || true; ... }` prints `{"b":2}`.
  - Because `-d ""` means every normal payload ends at EOF with rc=1, every wrapper test already exercises the non-zero-exit retention path.
  - The trailing newline is kept and `printf '%s\n'` adds a second one. This is harmless for JSON, and `sameJSON` accounts for it.
  - An embedded NUL would truncate the payload. JSON from Claude Code does not contain raw NULs.
- TestWrappersGiveEthosAFreshPipe (plugin/hooks/stdin_wrappers_test.go:~121-129, helper at :36-93) does prove a fresh pipe.
  - The wrapper's stdin is a `syscall.Socketpair` (:61), matching Node's socketpair stdin. The fake ethos runs `[ -p /dev/stdin ]`, which is true only for a FIFO.
  - A passthrough wrapper, whether `ethos hook x` or `< /dev/stdin`, would leave ethos with the socket. The fake would write "other" and the assertion would fail. The `cat > out` line also keeps the fake reading.
  - It is weaker than the dev/inode check the contract suggested. It asserts "is a pipe" rather than "is not the inherited fd". The socket-versus-FIFO difference makes it sufficient for this harness.

**2. Null persona**
- internal/mcp/tools.go:321-323 returns a non-error `noIdentity(caller)` text, "<agent_type> has no ethos identity", falling back to the agent_id only when no agent_type was recorded (caller.go:132-142). It happens before any `loadCallerIdentity` call. There is no fallback to leader, env, PID, git or OS on this path.
  - The same paths without a declared caller (tools.go:330 onward) are unchanged.
  - The declared-caller branch returns before `resolve.Resolve`.
- iam (tools.go:241-250) skips validating the caller's own empty persona and still calls `loadCallerIdentity(persona)` on the new one. A missing or invalid new persona is refused, and the test covers that. `SetExistingPersona` is keyed on the exact ref, so the leader's persona is untouched.
- doctor (caller.go:155-157) shows PASS with the same text.
- Roster and mission binding use only `callerParticipant` and never read `.Persona`. A grep of internal/mcp shows `.Persona` read only in tools.go and caller.go.
- The OpenCode `_meta` path goes through `requestCaller` (caller.go:64-67) to the same branch.
  - A persona-less OpenCode participant now gets "ses_X has no ethos identity" instead of an error. It opens no fallback, because the handler returns text and never consults another source.
  - Dropping `""` from TestMetadataCaller_InvalidPersona (caller_test.go:166) is justified by the new TestMetadataCaller_NoPersona.
- Agent-type default persona: the code has no config mapping. internal/hook/subagent_start.go:~178-182 matches an identity whose handle equals `agent_type`, which is DES-007's "Resolved: Persona Default by Agent Type". The docs say this correctly (docs/claude-code-mcp-identity.md, "Callers with no persona").

**3. Tests guard the claims**
- caller_hook_test.go: PersonaLessWhoami sets CLAUDE_PID, ETHOS_SESSION, ETHOS_AGENT_ID and USER to the leader and bob. It asserts `IsError` is false, that the text contains "no ethos identity" and "general-purpose", and that it does not contain alice, bob or carol.
  - A regression to the old error fails the first assertion, and a regression to leader or env fallback fails the NotContains check.
  - The agent_id-label subtest, the iam test (unknown persona refused, valid persona set, agent_type kept, leader unchanged, whoami then returns bob) and the roster, mission-session and doctor test are all adequate.
  - Fail-before is plausible: before, `loadCallerIdentity("")` returned `invalid caller persona ""`, which is the leader's e2e error.
- I did not run any test against the pre-change code.
- Wrapper tests: the stalled-writer test (8 KiB, then a 1.3s pause) would fail under `-t 1`, and the multiline and 100 KiB tests would fail under the old single-line read.

**Findings, ranked (all minor, none block acceptance)**
1. plugin/hooks/*.sh:9 — `read -t 10` is bounded at 10s only if the writer never closes. Claude Code ends stdin, so there is no cost in practice. If it ever fails to close, every PreToolUse call waits 10s, and the timeout path (a partial read kept after `-t` fires) has no test. This is low risk. A test with a writer that stays open past the timeout would pin DES-029's "partial input preserved" claim, but it would take 10s per wrapper.
2. internal/mcp/caller_hook_test.go (new tests) — mission binding for a persona-less caller is checked only through `callerSessionID`, not through a mission tool call at mission_tools.go:240 or :544. This is acceptable because those sites never read `.Persona`.
3. internal/mcp/caller.go:136-141 — `agent_type` comes from the hook payload and is echoed into tool text unsanitized. The hook is the trusted source and the roster is local, but it is untrusted-string reflection into model context. Low risk.
4. internal/hook/subagent_start.go:~176-182 — when `deps.Issue != nil` (identity store unusable) the subagent gets an empty persona. Callers now see "has no ethos identity" instead of an error, which hides a store fault. whoami still checks `ConfigIssue` first (tools.go:309), so a broken store is still reported for whoami. This is a design observation, not a regression.

Note that whoami's persona-less answer is plain text, not JSON. `formatIdentityDetail` (internal/hook/format_output.go:119-123) falls through to `emitSimple`, so the hook formatter handles it. Any machine consumer that parses whoami JSON must handle this case.

**Text for the leader to add to DESIGN.md (I did not edit it)**
- DES-029 "Decision" and "Why This Works" still show `IFS= read -r -t 1`, and say "The 1-second timeout matches the existing `ReadInput` timeout in Go". They should be amended. The shipped form is `read -r -d "" -t 10`: `-d ""` reads past newlines to EOF, which fixes the 8 KiB truncation. The timeout is 10s. EOF with rc=1 still leaves the data in the variable, which is the reason for initializing before the read.
- DES-007 should note that the "Null persona handling" query-tool behaviour is implemented as the text "<agent_type> has no ethos identity" in identity whoami and the doctor Human identity row. It uses the agent_id when no agent_type was recorded. A caller with no persona may declare one through iam.

tool_input.message:
I found 7 error-handling problems in `fix/mcp-caller-hook` vs `origin/main`. Worktree: `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller`. This was a read-only audit: I read the full non-test diff, `DESIGN.md` (DES-029 and both DES-074 2026-11-03 amendments), `resolve.SessionID` and `resolve.Resolve`, and `cmd/ethos/hook.go`. The one experiment I ran was a bash `read -t` timeout test with bash 5.2.21.

The core problem is findings 1 and 2. The server trusts `_caller`, and that trust depends on ethos's own hook running successfully on every ethos MCP call. When the hook fails or is bypassed, nothing is loud. The call goes through with the model's raw arguments, and the server then falls back to the env/PID resolution that the amendment exists to remove.

## 1. CRITICAL: any hook failure lets a model-supplied `_caller` through
**Where:** `plugin/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh:24-25` (`|| true` after the `ethos hook pre-tool-use` pipeline), `internal/hook/pretooluse.go:90-93`, `cmd/ethos/hook.go:230`, and `internal/hook/pretooluse_caller.go:30` and `:41` (the error returns).

**How it fails:** every error from `HandlePreToolUse` (a `ReadInput` parse error, a gate error, a JSON decode error) makes ethos exit non-zero. The wrapper's `|| true` turns that into exit 0 with empty stdout. Claude Code reads that as "no opinion" and runs the tool with the model's original `tool_input`.
- A model that put `_caller: {session_id: S, agent_id: <leader pid>}` in an `identity`/`iam` call has it delivered unchanged.
- `handleIam` (`tools.go`, the `requestCaller` block) then runs `SetExistingPersona(S, <leader>, persona)`. A subagent can rewrite the leader's persona, or `whoami` as another participant.

The amendment's claim that "a model-supplied value never survives" is only true when the hook succeeds.

**Concrete trigger:** an Edit-sized or otherwise large payload that stalls for more than 10s. The wrapper forwards the fragment (see finding 3), Go returns "invalid JSON input", and the call is let through.

**Fix:** the Go side can fail closed for ethos tools only. On a `ReadInput` error, check the raw bytes for `"tool_name":"mcp__plugin_ethos` (or regex-match the fragment's `tool_name`). If it matches, emit `deny` with a reason ("ethos hook could not read the payload; caller cannot be declared"). The handler errors at `pretooluse_caller.go:30/41` should emit a deny for the ethos tool, not return an error.

## 2. HIGH: when no caller is declared, the server falls back to env/PID/walk identity
**Where:**
- `internal/hook/pretooluse_caller.go:39` and `:65-74`: no caller and no spoof means a silent pass; no caller with a spoof means strip and pass.
- `internal/mcp/tools.go:623-628` (`callerSessionID` with no caller calls `resolve.SessionID`), `:609` (`resolveSessionID`), `:263` (`handleIam` with no caller calls `process.FindClaudePID()` and `JoinSelf`), `:330` (`handleWhoami` with no caller calls `identity.ForCaller` / `resolve.Resolve`), and `:706` (doctor keeps the env-derived row).

**How it fails:** the hook knows this is an ethos MCP call but cannot declare a caller. That happens when `CLAUDE_PID` fails corroboration, `session_id` is empty, the kill switch is set, `~/.punt-labs/ethos` is missing, `ethos` is not on PATH, or finding 1 applies. The call then reaches the server with no `_caller`, and the server takes the pre-amendment path. The amendment itself measures two outcomes of that path:
- **Nested `claude -p`:** the MCP server inherits the outer session's `CLAUDE_PID`, so `session roster` returns the outer session's roster and `bindDispatchedMission` writes the pending dispatch into the outer session. Both are silent.
- **Subagent call:** `handleIam` keys on `FindClaudePID()`, which is the leader. A subagent's `iam` silently overwrites the leader's persona, and `whoami` answers with the leader's identity. This is exactly the "falls back to the leader or to env, PID" outcome the persona-less amendment forbids.

"Without `_caller`, behavior is unchanged" is fine for non-Claude clients. Under Claude Code it reintroduces the silent wrong answer.

**Fix:**
- **Hook side:** when `declaredCaller` returns nil for an ethos tool, deny with the cause ("ethos: cannot declare the MCP caller: no session_id" / "CLAUDE_PID not corroborated"). At minimum, write it to stderr so it reaches `hook-errors.log`. Today this branch logs nothing.
- **Server side:** when `resolve.UnderClaudeCode()` is true and there is no `_caller` or `_meta`, refuse with a named error ("Claude Code call arrived without `_caller`; is the ethos PreToolUse hook installed and enabled?"). Do not call `resolve.SessionID`, `FindClaudePID`, or `resolve.Resolve`.

## 3. HIGH: a 10s stall forwards a partial payload, and the timeout looks like success
**Where:** all 8 wrappers, `IFS= read -r -d "" -t 10 HOOK_INPUT 2>/dev/null || true`. For example `plugin/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh:24`.

**Evidence (bash 5.2.21):**
```
(printf '{"a":'; sleep 3) | { IFS= read -r -d "" -t 1 X; echo "rc=$? [$X]"; }
rc=142 [{"a":]
```
- **Bash 5:** on timeout, bash keeps the partial input and returns rc 142 (above 128). `|| true` treats that the same as the normal EOF rc=1, and the fragment is forwarded as if complete. Go then rejects it as invalid JSON, the error goes to `hook-errors.log`, and the tool call proceeds. For an ethos MCP call that is finding 1.
- **Bash 3.2:** this is `/bin/bash` on macOS, which `#!/usr/bin/env bash` resolves to when Homebrew bash is not on PATH; one of the operator's hosts is macOS. Bash 3.2 is believed to discard partial input on timeout; I did not test this. If so, `HOOK_INPUT` stays empty, Go gets an empty map with no error (`parseJSON`, `stdin.go`), and `routePreToolUse` passes with no log at all.

**Fix:** capture the status, e.g. `IFS= read -r -d "" -t 10 HOOK_INPUT 2>/dev/null; rc=$?`. If `rc -gt 128`, write "ethos <hook>: stdin read timed out after 10s (N bytes)" to `hook-errors.log`. For `pre-tool-use`, either skip invoking ethos or pass a flag so Go can deny ethos tools. In Go, an empty payload reaching `HandlePreToolUse` should be logged, not passed silently.

## 4. MEDIUM: Go's `ReadInput` hides an empty timeout and its doc comment is stale
**Where:** `internal/hook/stdin.go:21-25` and `:44-70`.
- The doc comment still says "Returns an empty map on … timeout". A timeout with a fragment actually returns a parse error, and a timeout with zero bytes returns `{}, nil`, which callers cannot tell apart from "Claude sent nothing".
- A `readFromFile` read error other than timeout or EOF (for example EIO) is also absorbed by `break // EOF, timeout, or error — all fine` and parsed as if complete.

**Fix:** return a distinct sentinel (`ErrInputTimeout`) when the deadline fires, and wrap any non-EOF, non-timeout read error. That lets the PreToolUse caller fail closed for ethos tools.

## 5. MEDIUM: a declared-caller error is swallowed when the error check comes second
**Where:** `internal/mcp/mission_tools.go:251` and `:546`.

`callerSessionID` returns `requestCaller`/`callerParticipant` errors, which are never `ErrNotUnderClaudeCode`, so they correctly become warnings. But a call with no caller under Claude Code with no `CLAUDE_PID` (the normal MCP-server case per the amendment) also returns `ErrNoSession`. For mission close/abandon that becomes only a warning string, and the mission closes with the active-mission sidecar left in place.
- `clearClosedMissionBindings` returns `nil` (silent) on `ErrNotUnderClaudeCode`. If the server ever loses `CLAUDECODE`, sidecar clearing is skipped with no signal.

Finding 2's server-side refusal is the real fix. Short of that, a failure to clear on close should go in the payload as a top-level `error`, not a warning.

## 6. MEDIUM: doctor substitutes its row by display-string match
**Where:** `internal/mcp/tools.go:706`, `results[i].Name == "Human identity"`, with the same literal duplicated in `caller.go` (`declaredCallerResult`).

If `doctor` renames the row, the declared-caller result is silently dropped and the env/PID-derived row stands. That is the same fallback as finding 2, and no test or compile error would catch it. Export the name as a constant from `internal/doctor` and fail loudly (or append a row) when no row matches.

## 7. LOW: injection is keyed on the plugin tool name only
**Where:** `internal/hook/pretooluse_caller.go:15` (`^mcp__plugin_ethos(-dev)?_self__`).

If ethos's server is registered any other way (a user `.mcp.json`, `claude mcp add ethos …`, giving `mcp__ethos__*`), the hook neither injects nor strips. The schema still advertises `_caller`, so a model value goes through. Today only the plugin path is documented, but nothing refuses the other path. Either document it as unsupported, or match on the server name `self` plus the tool set.

## Done correctly
- `requestCaller` refuses a call that sets both `_caller` and `_meta`.
- `parseCallerArg` rejects unknown keys and unsafe IDs and requires both fields; an invalid caller never falls back.
- `callerParticipant` requires one exact `agent_id` and detects duplicates.
- A gate `deny` stands over injection (`pretooluse_caller.go:39`).
- Removing `"allow"` (`preToolUsePass`) is correct.
- `routePreToolUse`'s `tierBRepoRoot` failure denies with a named reason rather than falling back.

tool_input.message:
Invariant audit of fix/mcp-caller-hook against origin/main, in <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller. Read-only. Two claims fail; the other four hold, three of them with gaps in what enforces them.

## Summary

| # | Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PreToolUse emits only deny or no decision | HOLDS (MEDIUM: nothing structural enforces it) |
| 2 | Hook always overwrites `_caller`; a model value never survives | FAILS (CRITICAL) |
| 3 | Every caller-dependent MCP method reads `_caller` | HOLDS today (HIGH: no test would catch a new method) |
| 4 | No env/PID/git/OS fallback when `_caller` is present | HOLDS (MEDIUM: the "no caller" case falls back) |
| 5 | Every `plugin/hooks/*.sh` wrapper reads stdin in bash and forwards a fresh pipe | HOLDS for the 8 Claude Code wrappers; the literal "every" is too broad |
| 6 | The named tests guard these properties | FAILS in part |

## Claim 1 — "ethos's PreToolUse hook emits deny or no permission decision": HOLDS (MEDIUM)

Every output path:
- `internal/hook/pretooluse.go` uses three constructors:
  - `preToolUsePass` (:34) and `preToolUsePassWithEnv` (:41) set no decision.
  - `preToolUseDeny` (:48) sets "deny".
- `routePreToolUse` writes only those: :120, :125, :129, :135, :143, :148, :171, :177.
- `pretooluse_dispatch.go:701,710,919` use the PassWithEnv constructor; `:1121` uses Deny.
- `pretooluse_caller.go:44` echoes the gate buffer; `:54` builds a result with only `HookEventName` and `UpdatedInput`.
- Error returns write nothing, and the wrapper's `|| true` turns that into no decision.
- No "allow" literal is left anywhere in `internal/hook`.

The gap: `preToolUseOutput.PermissionDecision` (:24) is a free `string`. Nothing stops a future `PermissionDecision: "allow"` except whichever tests happen to reach that path.
- `TestPreToolUse_PassThroughNeverDecidesPermission` (`pretooluse_passthrough_test.go:16`) checks 7 hardcoded payloads.
- The rewritten `pretooluse_test.go` and `pretooluse_dispatch_test.go` assertions do reach every current pass path (:148, the extract-into pass at :171, tier A and tier B).
- **Fix:** make the decision a type that can only be empty or deny (for example an unexported `denyDecision bool` that is marshalled to "deny"). Or add an AST test that fails on any `PermissionDecision` assignment other than "deny".

## Claim 2 — "the hook always overwrites a model-supplied `_caller`, and strips it when no caller can be determined": FAILS (CRITICAL)

Inside `handleEthosMCPCall` (`pretooluse_caller.go:27-58`) the claim holds:
- Deny: the gate buffer is echoed and the call is blocked.
- No caller and no `_caller` in the input: the call passes through unchanged.
- Caller found: `_caller` is overwritten (:49).
- No caller but a `_caller` in the input: it is deleted (:51).
- `TestPreToolUse_OverwritesModelSuppliedCaller` and `TestPreToolUse_NoCallerStripsSpoofedCaller` cover these branches.

The claim fails on every path where the Go function produces no output, because then Claude Code runs the call with its original input:
1. **Wrapper bypasses** in `plugin/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh`, each of which exits 0 with no output:
   - `$HOME/.punt-hooks-kill` exists;
   - `$HOME/.punt-labs/ethos` is missing;
   - `ethos` is not on the hook's PATH (the MCP server can still be running from the plugin manifest).
2. **Handler errors** also produce no output, which the wrapper's `|| true` passes through:
   - `ReadInput` fails (`pretooluse.go:90-92`), for example a payload truncated by the 10 s bash read;
   - `routePreToolUse` or the gate `json.Unmarshal` fails (`pretooluse_caller.go:29-35`).

The server cannot tell the hook's value from the model's (`caller.go:57-73`, `parseCallerArg`), and it trusts whatever arrives.
- **Falsifying case:** touch `~/.punt-hooks-kill`, then have the model call `mcp__plugin_ethos_self__session` with `{method:"iam", persona:"x", _caller:{session_id:<other>, agent_id:<other>}}`.
- `handleIam` (`tools.go:216-252`) calls `SetExistingPersona(ref.sessionID, ref.agentID, persona)` on someone else's participant.
- `whoami` returns another participant's identity in the same way.
- `TestWrappersBypasses` (`stdin_wrappers_test.go`) actually asserts this no-output bypass, so the gap is tested in, not guarded against.

The DESIGN.md sentence "The hook always overwrites `_caller`, so a model-supplied value never survives" is false as written. The "Routing, not authentication" paragraph covers only clients that are not Claude Code; it does not cover Claude Code running with the hook bypassed or failing.

**Fix (one of):**
- When the tool name matches `ethosMCPTool`, make the wrapper and handler fail closed: emit deny if the hook cannot run or errors.
- Or have the hook authenticate `_caller` (for example an HMAC with a per-user secret under `~/.punt-labs/ethos` that the server checks), so an unsigned `_caller` is refused.

**Unverified dependency:** stripping only works if Claude Code replaces the tool input with `updatedInput` rather than merging it.
- DESIGN.md measured injection ("the injected argument reaches the server").
- It did not measure removal, and no test or doc in the diff covers it.
- If Claude Code merges, the strip branch (:51) has no effect.

## Claim 3 — "every caller-dependent MCP method consults `_caller`": HOLDS today (HIGH)

Every tool registered in `RegisterTools` (`tools.go:140-172`), and every place that resolves a session or identity:

| Method | How it reads the caller |
|---|---|
| identity whoami | `requestCaller`, `tools.go:313` |
| session iam | `tools.go:216`, after `resolveSessionID` |
| session roster/join/leave (no explicit `session_id`) | `resolveSessionID`, `tools.go:579-598` |
| doctor, Human identity row | `tools.go:701-710` |
| mission create | `bindDispatchedMission`, `mission_tools.go:240` via `callerSessionID` |
| mission close / abandon | `clearClosedMissionBindings`, `mission_tools.go:544` |

None of the other tools resolve the caller:
- identity list/get/create, ext, the attribute tools, role and vendor take no caller.
- team `for_repo` reads only repo location (`team_tools.go:223`).
- ADR author is a plain argument.
- mission advance uses the contract's Leader (`mission_tools.go:659`).
- correct, result and reflect take author from the YAML.
- `ClearMissionBindings` (`internal/mission/active.go:907`) uses only the session ID it is given.

Nothing enforces this for the future.
- `TestDeclaredCaller_SchemaEntries` (`caller_hook_test.go:285`) checks a hardcoded list of 4 tools.
- No test fails if a new handler calls `resolve.SessionID`, `resolve.Resolve`, `process.*` or `os.Getenv("ETHOS_*")` without going through `requestCaller`.
- Example: a new mission method that calls `resolve.SessionID(h.sessionStore)` directly reintroduces the nested-session wrong-roster bug, and every test still passes.
- **Fix:** an AST or grep test over `internal/mcp/*.go`. It should allow `resolve.SessionID`, `resolve.Resolve`, `process.*` and `ETHOS_AGENT_ID`/`ETHOS_SESSION` reads only inside the no-caller branches of `callerSessionID`, `resolveSessionID`, `handleIam` and `handleWhoami`. Better still, route all of them through one function.

## Claim 4 — "nothing falls back to env, PID, git or OS identity when `_caller` is present": HOLDS (MEDIUM)

- Each present-branch returns before any fallback: `tools.go:216-253` (iam), `313-328` (whoami), `581-600` (`resolveSessionID`), `624-636` (`callerSessionID`).
- An invalid caller is "present with an error" (`caller.go:62-72`), so it never reaches a fallback either.
- `TestDeclaredCaller_NoFallback` and `TestDeclaredCaller_Malformed` check this with misleading `ETHOS_SESSION` and `ETHOS_AGENT_ID` set.

Doctor is the exception in mechanics, not in output:
- `doctor.RunAllFor` still computes the Human identity row through `resolve.Resolve` (`internal/doctor/doctor.go:1215`, which runs the env/PID/git/OS chain).
- `tools.go:704-709` then replaces it by matching the name "Human identity". That string is written three times: `doctor.go:1213`, `caller.go` (`declaredCallerResult`), and `tools.go:705`.
- If doctor renamed the row, `TestDeclaredCaller_Doctor` would fail (it asserts "Repo carol (carol)"), so this is guarded.
- **Fix:** share the name as a constant, or pass the declared caller into `RunAllFor` so the fallback never runs.

Related gap (MEDIUM): when the hook cannot determine a caller it strips `_caller`, and the server then takes the no-caller path, which is the env/`CLAUDE_PID` chain (`tools.go:626`, `609`, `260-263`, `331`).
- In the nested `claude -p` case the amendment describes, that chain is exactly the one that returned the outer session's roster.
- So "no caller" leads to the silent wrong answer, not an error.
- **Fix:** when the hook sees a Claude Code payload but cannot determine a caller, inject a marker such as `_caller: null` (or deny), so the server refuses rather than falling back.

## Claim 5 — "every plugin/hooks/*.sh wrapper reads stdin in bash and forwards a fresh pipe" (DES-029): HOLDS for the wrappers it means

- All 8 hooks.json command wrappers read stdin in bash with `IFS= read -r -d "" -t 10 HOOK_INPUT ... || true`, then run `printf '%s\n' "$HOOK_INPUT" | ethos hook <sub> ... || true`:
  - audit-log, pre-compact, pre-tool-use, session-end, session-start, subagent-start, subagent-stop, suppress-output.
- `commit-msg.sh` and `pre-commit.sh` match the glob but are git hooks that read no stdin. Taken literally, "every `plugin/hooks/*.sh`" is false. Scope the wording to "every hooks.json wrapper".
- The test does not prevent drift: `stdinWrappers` (`stdin_wrappers_test.go:21-30`) is a hardcoded map, not read from `hooks.json`. A new wrapper added to `hooks.json` that passes inherited stdin straight to Go would not be tested.
  - **Fix:** build the list by parsing `hooks.json` command entries, and assert the map matches it exactly.
- The two test suites assume different Claude Code behaviour:
  - `stdin_stall_test.go` says "The write end stays open: no EOF, as with Claude Code".
  - The wrapper's `read -d ""` only returns before 10 s on EOF, and `runWrapper` closes the write end.
  - If Claude Code really never sends EOF, every hook call waits the full 10 s.
  - The DESIGN.md line "the shell and Go bounds agree" is only partly true: Go returns as soon as the JSON is complete; bash does not.
  - Pick one EOF model and test the wrapper against it.

## Claim 6 — do the tests named in the 2026-11-03 amendments catch a regression?

- **`TestWrappersGiveEthosAFreshPipe`** (the only test DESIGN.md names): catches a regression in the 8 listed wrappers. A wrapper passing the inherited socketpair shows up as "other", not "pipe". It misses any new wrapper (HIGH, above).
- **DES-074 amendment tests:**
  - `pretooluse_caller_test.go` covers overwrite, strip, deny standing, and the ethos-tool name match (including a lookalike and another server).
  - `caller_hook_test.go` covers the server side well.
  - None covers the wrapper-bypass or handler-error paths, where the CRITICAL gap is.
  - `TestDeclaredCaller_SchemaEntries` uses a fixed list of tools (HIGH).
- **"PreToolUse never decides allow" amendment:** the reachable pass paths are covered today. The free-string type leaves future paths unguarded (MEDIUM).

## Files

- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/internal/hook/pretooluse_caller.go
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/internal/hook/pretooluse.go
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/plugin/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/plugin/hooks/stdin_wrappers_test.go
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/internal/mcp/caller.go
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/internal/mcp/tools.go
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/internal/mcp/mission_tools.go
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/internal/mcp/caller_hook_test.go
- <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller/internal/doctor/doctor.go

Review of fix/mcp-caller-hook against origin/main (worktree <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-caller). 35 files. I read every non-test code change: internal/hook/{pretooluse.go, pretooluse_caller.go, pretooluse_dispatch.go, stdin.go, the ReadInput call sites}, internal/mcp/{caller.go, tools.go, mission_tools.go}, all 8 plugin/hooks/*.sh wrappers, plugin/hooks/stdin_wrappers_test.go, docs/claude-code-mcp-identity.md, and the DESIGN.md amendments dated 2026-11-03 (DES-007, DES-029, DES-074, DES-054). `go test -count=1 ./internal/hook/ ./internal/mcp/ ./plugin/hooks/` passes.

**No findings at confidence 80 or above.** The four changes do what the 2026-11-03 amendments say:

1. **Hook injects or strips `_caller`.** `handleEthosMCPCall` (pretooluse_caller.go:187-218) runs the normal gates first and keeps a deny as it is. If there is no caller and no model-supplied `_caller`, the gate output passes through unchanged. Otherwise it returns `updatedInput`, copying the input and then overwriting or deleting `_caller`. A model-supplied `_caller` set to `null` is also stripped, because the presence check uses the map key.
2. **Server resolves `_caller` by exact participant.** `requestCaller`/`parseCallerArg` (caller.go:58-102) reject unknown keys, non-string values, empty values and unsafe IDs. They also refuse a request that carries both `_meta` and `_caller`. `callerParticipant` looks up the exact agent_id with no fallback. A persona-less caller follows DES-007 in whoami, doctor and iam; iam skips validating the empty existing persona. I checked that the doctor row name "Human identity" matches internal/doctor/doctor.go:1213. Plain-text whoami output goes through `formatIdentityDetail`'s `emitSimple` fallback, so the PostToolUse formatter does not break. No MCP handler walks all its arguments or decodes them strictly, so injecting `_caller` into tools that do not declare it (team, role, ext, …) is harmless.
3. **No "allow" left.** I grepped internal/, cmd/ and plugin/ for `"allow"` and `PermissionDecision:`. The only decision left is `"deny"` at pretooluse.go:51, and `omitempty` drops the empty field.
4. **Stdin handling.** The wrappers use `read -r -d "" -t 10` and still pipe to ethos rather than handing it the inherited fd. Both Go read paths (deadline and goroutine) stop as soon as the buffer is valid JSON, under one 10s bound. Every `ReadInput` call site now uses `hookInputTimeout`.

**Below threshold (about 70). Not counted as findings, but worth a decision:**

- **pretooluse_caller.go:229-236: a subagent can be attributed to the leader without any error.** `declaredCaller` uses the corroborated `CLAUDE_PID` whenever the payload has no `agent_id`.
  - Failure scenario: a Claude Code version whose SubagentStart payload has `agent_id` (so the subagent is in the roster) but whose PreToolUse payload does not. On that version a subagent's call is sent as the leader. `identity whoami` returns the leader's persona. A subagent's `session iam` calls `SetExistingPersona` on the leader's participant and overwrites the leader's persona.
  - Before this branch the same call failed with ErrNoSession. Now it returns a wrong answer with no error, which the DES-074 no-fallback rule exists to prevent.
  - The amendment measured 2.1.309 only. Neither the design doc nor the code states a minimum Claude Code version.
  - Suggested fix: state the minimum version in docs/claude-code-mcp-identity.md. Better, add a guard: when the payload has `agent_type` but no `agent_id`, declare no caller and strip `_caller` instead of falling back to the leader's PID.
- **pretooluse.go:106-110 / pretooluse_caller.go:189-191: on a hook error, a model-supplied `_caller` gets through.** If `HandlePreToolUse` returns an error for an ethos MCP call, the wrapper's `|| true` exits 0 with no output. The original input goes through, including any model-supplied `_caller`. Two things can cause this: a `routePreToolUse` error, such as the `tierBRepoRoot` failure under a verifier allowlist, or an unparseable payload. The amendment says the hook is "the only place this can be enforced". The same applies when the `~/.punt-hooks-kill` switch is set. The "routing, not authentication" section of the amendment already accepts this, so it is listed here only for completeness.

Mission m-2026-11-04-002 round 1 is submitted with verdict pass. F1–F6 and Qodo Q1 are done in 5 commits on fix/mcp-caller-hook. Q2 (Qodo "disabled repos still run hook work") is not implemented because it conflicts with the standard; it needs a ruling (below). `make check` passed in full, and I read the output, on every commit. Nothing was pushed.

## ADRs read first
I read DES-007 (the "Null persona handling" text at DESIGN.md:368), DES-029 with its 2026-11-03 amendment (1859–2028), DES-054 (4899ff), DES-061 R4 (6430–6444) and DES-074 in full with both 2026-11-03 amendments (7926–9038). No conflict with F1–F6. Q2 conflicts as described below.

## Commits (worktree .claude/worktrees/mcp-caller)

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| 6a36077 | `fix(hook)`: F3 and Q1, in `internal/hook/stdin.go` and `stdin_test.go` |
| e67c1ea | `fix(hook)`: F2 and F6a, in `pretooluse.go`, `pretooluse_caller.go` and tests |

| 14ef95a | docs: CHANGELOG and `docs/claude-code-mcp-identity.md` |

## What each item does
- **F1:** `nocaller.go` holds all no-caller resolution. Under `resolve.UnderClaudeCode()` with no `_caller` or `_meta`, every caller-dependent method returns the named error.
  - It is `errNoCaller`, a type with the exact text, because staticcheck ST1005 rejects `errors.New("Claude…")` and suppressions are forbidden.
  - Methods covered: `whoami`, `roster`/`join`/`leave` without `session_id`, `iam` (even with `session_id`), mission binding, and the doctor Human identity row.
  - Explicit `session_id` admin targets still work. Non-Claude-Code clients keep the old chain.
  - Doctor: `doctor.HumanIdentityRow` is a shared constant, and `RunAllForCaller` takes the caller's row so no env-derived row is ever computed.
- **F2:**
  - A read, parse, route or gate-decode failure on an ethos MCP tool now denies with the cause in the reason and on stderr. It was an error with no output.
  - An unparseable payload is still denied if its raw bytes match `"tool_name":"mcp__plugin_ethos(-dev)?_self__…"`. Other tools keep the old error.
  - `agent_type` with no `agent_id` declares no caller.
  - Every no-caller cause is logged to stderr.
- **F3:**
  - `ErrInputTimeout` is returned with the byte count, and non-EOF read errors are wrapped. The stale doc comment is rewritten.
  - A zero-byte timeout is now an error too. Previously it was an empty map.
  - All hook handlers already returned the `ReadInput` error, so they log it.
- **Q1:**
  - An early return happens only on a complete top-level object. A proper prefix of an object is never valid JSON.
  - Trailing bytes in the same read make the buffer invalid, so the read continues to EOF or the deadline and the payload is refused.
  - Bytes arriving in a later, separate write after a complete object are not read. That is the one-payload-per-hook protocol.
  - Most Q1 tests are guards that passed before the change, so only the timeout/error ones have fail-before evidence.
- **F4:** Each wrapper sets `_rc=0`, captures read's status, and on a value above 128 appends `ethos <hook>: stdin read timed out after 10s (N bytes)` to `hook-errors.log`. It then forwards as before. Shellcheck is clean.
- **F5:** A failure to clear bindings on close or abandon now returns an error result. It names the mission, its terminal status, "may still stamp commit trailers", and every cause. The status change stands.
- **F6a:** `permissionDecision` is an unexported bool type. It marshals only to `"deny"`, omitted when false, and unmarshalling `"allow"` is an error. `Decision()` returns the string form, and about 70 test assertions were switched to it.
- **F6b:** `TestNoCallerResolutionLivesInOneFile` is an AST scan with import-alias awareness. It fails if the banned `resolve`/`process` selectors or the `ETHOS_SESSION`/`ETHOS_AGENT_ID` literals appear outside `nocaller.go`. A scanner self-test proves it detects each one.
- **F6c:** `stdinWrappers(t)` is read from `hooks.json` and must equal the set of `*.sh` files that run `ethos hook`.
- **Docs:** CHANGELOG and `docs/claude-code-mcp-identity.md` are updated. `npx markdownlint-cli2` on both files returned zero findings.

## Fail-before evidence
- Hook: with `refuseUnreadable` returning the cause, and the `agent_type` guard disabled, `TestPreToolUse_UnreadablePayloadForEthosToolDenies` fails 4 subtests and `TestPreToolUse_AgentTypeWithoutAgentIDDeclaresNoCaller` fails.
- Wrappers: against the HEAD~ wrappers, `TestWrappersLogAStdinReadTimeout` fails for all 8.
- MCP: with `refuseUndeclared` returning nil, `TestNoCaller_*` fail across whoami, session roster/join/leave/iam, doctor row, and mission create/close/abandon. Each test also has a non-Claude-Code control.
- `ErrInputTimeout`, `Decision()` and `HumanIdentityRow` did not exist, so their tests fail to compile before the change.

## Q2 conflict: not implemented, needs a ruling
- The standard (`~/Coding/punt-labs/punt-kit/standards/tool-enable-disable.md:287-295`) prescribes the literal gate `[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.punt-labs/<tool>/enabled" ] || exit 0`. On `pre-tool-use.sh` that skips `_caller` injection, which F1 now refuses server-side. It also skips the Agent dispatch env block (`DELEGATION_ID`, `MISSION_ID`, `internal/hook/pretooluse.go` around lines 130–160) and the verifier allowlist gate.
- Ethos has never gated its plugin hooks on the marker. `docs/enable-disable.md:291-311` ("The §2.7 marker gate") and DES-059 (DESIGN.md:6242-6314) scope the gate to the two git hooks, `pre-commit.sh` and `commit-msg.sh`. All 8 plugin wrappers gate only on the kill switch, `~/.punt-labs/ethos` and the `ethos` binary on PATH.
- Gating only `pre-tool-use.sh` would be inconsistent with the other seven wrappers. It would also let a verifier's write fence lapse in a dormant repo.
- Recommendation: do not gate. Answer the Qodo finding as "plugin hooks are user-scoped by design (DES-059; docs/enable-disable.md:291-311)". If the operator wants marker-gating of plugin hooks, that is a design change for its own bead and covers all 8 wrappers.
- A compatible split would be: a bash match on the raw payload for an ethos MCP `tool_name` runs the hook, and any other tool exits 0 when the marker is absent. The Go side would still need `resolve.EnabledMarker` plus the verifier-fence question settled first.

## Other points for the leader
- **F1 on `mission create`:** the named error goes in `warnings` and the mission is still created, because it exists. Close and abandon return an error. Contract F5 only names close/abandon, so confirm this.
- **Contract test line "kill-switch + model `_caller` → server refuses":** this holds only for invalid `_caller` values. The server cannot tell a model-written well-formed `_caller` naming a real participant from the hook's, and DES-074 says "routing, not authentication". `TestNoCaller_ForgedCallerWithoutHookIsStillChecked` pins that unknown participants, unknown sessions and malformed values are refused and never fall back to the environment.
- **Risk in F2's `agent_type` rule:** per the hooks docs, a `claude --agent X` main-thread payload carries `agent_type` without `agent_id`. Such a session would then get no `_caller` and be refused on every ethos MCP call. I did not verify this live. If it is real, the alternative is to key on the leader's `CLAUDE_PID` when `agent_type` equals the session's agent.
- **Stray audit message:** `PostToolUse` logged `reading input: invalid JSON input (65536 bytes)` for my own Edit. That is the installed binary's old read path. It is not part of this diff.
- **Scratch files:** `.tmp/` in the worktree holds my backups and the result YAML. It is gitignored.

## DESIGN.md text to add (I did not edit it)

Add under DES-074:

> ### Amendment 2026-11-03: the server fails closed, and so does the hook
>
> **The gap.** The first amendment made the PreToolUse hook the only declarer of the caller, but left the server's old chain in place for a call that arrives without `_caller`. With the hook missing, disabled (`~/.punt-hooks-kill`), crashed, or unable to declare a caller, a Claude Code call fell through to `ETHOS_SESSION`/`ETHOS_AGENT_ID` and the process tree. An MCP server has no `CLAUDE_PID` and outlives its sessions, so that chain can answer with another session's identity and no error. That is the plausible wrong answer this decision exists to close.
>
> **Decision.** (1) Under Claude Code, a caller-dependent method with neither `_caller` nor OpenCode `_meta` returns a named error: "Claude Code call arrived without _caller: the ethos PreToolUse hook did not declare the caller (is it installed, enabled, and not killed?)". It never reads `resolve.SessionID`, `resolve.Resolve`, `process.FindClaudePID` or `ETHOS_*`. Explicit `session_id` admin targets and non-Claude-Code clients are unchanged. All no-caller resolution lives in `internal/mcp/nocaller.go`, and `TestNoCallerResolutionLivesInOneFile` fails if those calls appear elsewhere in the package. Doctor's Human identity row is supplied by the caller (`doctor.RunAllForCaller`, row name `doctor.HumanIdentityRow`), so no env-derived row can stand. (2) For ethos MCP tools the hook denies, naming the cause, when it cannot read, parse or route the payload (a payload too broken to parse is still denied if its raw bytes name an ethos MCP `tool_name`), instead of exiting with an error and no output (which Claude Code reads as "proceed"). A payload with `agent_type` but no `agent_id` declares no caller, since `CLAUDE_PID` would name the leader. (3) `ReadInput` returns `ErrInputTimeout` when the deadline fires, wraps other read errors, and treats only a complete top-level object as a whole payload. (4) Mission close/abandon return an error result when the bindings cannot be cleared, because the close stands but a surviving sidecar keeps stamping the closed mission. (5) The PreToolUse permission decision is a type that holds deny or nothing. "Allow" cannot be expressed.
>
> **Rejected:** keep the env chain for a caller-less Claude Code call and log it (a log is not a refusal); deny every call when no caller can be declared (the server refuses the ones that need a caller, and the rest need none).
>
> **Not changed:** `_caller` is routing, not authentication. A well-formed `_caller` naming a real participant is routed whoever wrote it.

Add to DES-029's 2026-11-03 amendment: "A wrapper whose `read -t 10` times out (status above 128) appends `ethos <hook>: stdin read timed out after 10s (N bytes)` to `hook-errors.log` and forwards what arrived. The wrapper list under test is read from `hooks.json`."

Add to DES-054's allow amendment: "The output type is `permissionDecision`, an unexported bool that marshals only to `"deny"`, so `allow` cannot be written."
